title: A new model for standardising and treating thermal injury in the rat
author: Davenport, Dobson, et al.

steps.title: Obtain and house rats
steps.instruction: Acquire ten adult male Sprague‑Dawley rats (320–340 g) from the JCU breeding colony, house them under a 14 h light/10 h dark cycle with ad libitum food and water.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and analgesia
steps.instruction: Place the rat in a nose cone and induce anesthesia with 5 % isoflurane in oxygen; maintain anesthesia with 0.5–1.5 % isoflurane while confirming loss of withdrawal reflex and stable heart rate, and administer buprenorphine hydrochloride (Temgesic) subcutaneously at 0.05 mg kg⁻¹ between the shoulder blades.

steps.title: Prepare skin surface
steps.instruction: Shave the dorsal, lateral, and left inguinal regions using clippers and Veet depilatory cream; disinfect the area with povidone‑iodine solution and wipe with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Maintain core body temperature
steps.instruction: Place the anesthetized rat on a Physitemp homeothermic blanket, insert a rectal T‑type probe, and adjust the blanket to keep core temperature between 35.5 °C and 37.5 °C throughout the experiment.

steps.title: Implant femoral vascular catheters
steps.instruction: Implant sterile chronic catheters (Access Technologies) into the left femoral artery and vein using a dual‑access vascular port (Walker Scientific): make a 12 mm transverse incision on the dorsal neck above the shoulder blades, create a subcutaneous pocket to the hips by blunt dissection; make a second incision in the left inguinal area, bluntly dissect the subcutaneous space, insert catheters, flush with heparinised saline, and close both incisions with 4‑0 braided silk suture. Connect the arterial catheter to a pressure transducer and Bridge Amplifier/PowerLab for continuous blood pressure monitoring, and attach subcutaneous ECG leads to fore‑ and hind‑limb paws.

steps.title: Stabilize animal before baseline
steps.instruction: Keep the animal under anesthesia for a 30‑min stabilization period, then record baseline physiological measurements.
